sentences.en: Late October, AD 130.
sentences.zh: 公元130年，十月下旬。

sentences.en: The body of a young man, still not twenty, was found floating in the Nile.
sentences.zh: 一名尚未满二十岁的年轻男子的尸体被发现漂浮在尼罗河上。

sentences.en: Hauled out from the river, dragged through the silt left by the retreating floodwaters, the corpse was brought to dry land.
sentences.zh: 尸体被打捞上岸，拖过洪水退去后留下的淤泥，被安置在干燥的土地上。

sentences.en: It was clear that the drowned man had been a figure strikingly out of the ordinary.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，这名溺水者绝非寻常之辈。

sentences.en: His body was gym-toned.
sentences.zh: 他的身体有着健身般的线条。

sentences.en: His proportions were perfect.
sentences.zh: 他的比例堪称完美。

sentences.en: His face possessed a heart-stopping, almost supernatural beauty.
sentences.zh: 他的面容拥有一种令人窒息、近乎超凡脱俗的美。

sentences.en: Who was he?
sentences.zh: 他是谁？

sentences.en: A foreigner, clearly.
sentences.zh: 显然是个外国人。

sentences.en: Yet the stretch of the Nile in which he had drowned was hardly the haunt of glamorous foreigners.
sentences.zh: 然而，他溺水的这段尼罗河河段，绝非那些光鲜亮丽的外国人会去的地方。

sentences.en: Alexandria lay far to the north.
sentences.zh: 亚历山大港远在北方。

sentences.en: Although there was an ancient temple adorned with squat pillars and the carvings of a forgotten pharaoh looming over the waters in which the young man had drowned,
sentences.zh: 尽管在那年轻人溺水的河水上方，矗立着一座古老的神庙，装饰着矮粗的柱子和被遗忘的法老的雕刻，

sentences.en: the building did not feature prominently in the roster of Egypt's tourist attractions.
sentences.zh: 但这座建筑在埃及的旅游景点名录中并不显眼。

sentences.en: Nothing stood beside it, save a scruffy village.
sentences.zh: 除了一个破败的村庄，周围空无一物。

sentences.en: Yet here, to this obscure and rural spot,
sentences.zh: 然而就在这里，在这个偏僻的乡村角落，

sentences.en: Caesar himself had come.
sentences.zh: 凯撒本人亲临了。

sentences.en: Caesar, who ruled in Egypt as pharaoh, at once king and living god.
sentences.zh: 凯撒，作为法老统治着埃及，既是国王，也是在世的神。

sentences.en: His barge, together with a great flotilla of other vessels, stood moored in the shallows of the temple.
sentences.zh: 他的御船，连同其他船只组成的庞大船队，停泊在神庙的浅滩处。

sentences.en: Clearly, then, the young man found in the Nile could only have been of his party.
sentences.zh: 那么很显然，在尼罗河中发现的这名年轻人，只能是他随行人员中的一员。

sentences.en: And so it proved.
sentences.zh: 事实也确实如此。

sentences.en: So that absolutely brilliant prose, Tom, which is from your forthcoming book, Pax.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，那段极其精彩的散文，出自你即将出版的新书《Pax》。

sentences.en: This is absolutely not the third time I've had to record this sentence because you were displeased with the original iterations.
sentences.zh: 这绝对不是我第三次录制这段话，只是因为你对最初的版本不满意。

sentences.en: I want nothing but the best for the listeners.
sentences.zh: 我只想为听众呈现最好的内容。

sentences.en: I want them to know that Pax is now available for pre-order in the UK.
sentences.zh: 我想让他们知道《Pax》现在已经在英国开启预售了。

sentences.en: But this is not about advertising.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是为了做广告。

sentences.en: This is about a dramatic episode in history.
sentences.zh: 这是关于历史上一个戏剧性的插曲。

sentences.en: Listeners can draw their own conclusions.
sentences.zh: 听众们可以得出自己的结论。

sentences.en: Tom, tell us about the mystery.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，给我们讲讲这个谜团吧。

sentences.en: Make the mystery sound exciting so people will buy your book as you're so keen for them to do.
sentences.zh: 把这个谜团讲得刺激一点，这样人们就会买你的书，毕竟你那么渴望他们去买。

sentences.en: Dominic, it's not about buying books.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，这与买书无关。

sentences.en: It's about marking Pride Month, which is happening in the UK at the moment and has become almost like a kind of religious carnival.
sentences.zh: 这是为了纪念“骄傲月”，它目前正在英国进行，已经演变成了一种宗教狂欢。

sentences.en: So we're doing two episodes.
sentences.zh: 所以我们要做两期节目。

sentences.en: The next one is going to be on Oscar Wilde, who is a martyr.
sentences.zh: 下一期将讲述奥斯卡·王尔德，他是一位殉道者。

sentences.en: But today, we are looking at a god because the young man who has been found floating in the waters of the Nile is indeed of Caesar's party.
sentences.zh: 但今天，我们要探讨一位神，因为那名被发现漂浮在尼罗河水中的年轻人，确实是凯撒随行人员中的一员。

sentences.en: And Caesar is the Emperor Hadrian.
sentences.zh: 而凯撒就是哈德良皇帝。

sentences.en: And Hadrian will be so devastated by the loss of this young man that he makes him into a god.
sentences.zh: 哈德良会因失去这个年轻人而悲痛欲绝，以至于将他封为神。

sentences.en: And so there are all kinds of mysteries that surround this episode.
sentences.zh: 所以，围绕这一事件有着各种各样的谜团。

sentences.en: I mean, most obviously, how has he drowned?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，最显而易见的是，他是怎么溺水的？

sentences.en: What's happened to him?
sentences.zh: 他发生了什么事？

sentences.en: But also, what is the nature of his relationship with Hadrian?
sentences.zh: 但还有，他与哈德良的关系本质上是什么？

sentences.en: And what is it about him?
sentences.zh: 他身上究竟有什么特质？

sentences.en: The cult of this young man, a Greek by the name of Antinous, becomes hugely successful.
sentences.zh: 这个年轻人的崇拜，一个名叫安提诺乌斯的希腊人，变得极其成功。

sentences.en: Hugely successful.
sentences.zh: 极其成功。

sentences.en: What is it about him that makes him such a striking figure?
sentences.zh: 他身上有什么特质使他成为如此引人注目的人物？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it's not just one of the great Roman mysteries, it's one of the great Roman love stories.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅是伟大的罗马谜团之一，也是伟大的罗马爱情故事之一。

sentences.en: Or is love story the right description?
sentences.zh: 或者说“爱情故事”这个描述准确吗？

sentences.en: Well, we can discuss that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们可以讨论一下。

sentences.en: So the setting is a kind of a heyday of the Roman Empire.
sentences.zh: 故事背景是罗马帝国的全盛时期。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Hadrian, best known in Britain for his war.
sentences.zh: 而哈德良，在英国最出名的是他的战争。

sentences.en: He becomes emperor in 117.
sentences.zh: 他在117年成为皇帝。

sentences.en: He is famously the first emperor to wear a beard.
sentences.zh: 他是有名的第一位留胡子的皇帝。

sentences.en: The first kind of ruler of the Near East to wear a beard since the time of Alexander the Great.
sentences.zh: 自亚历山大大帝时代以来，第一位留胡子的近东统治者。

sentences.en: Because Alexander the Great obviously set the fashion for clean shaving.
sentences.zh: 因为亚历山大大帝显然引领了刮胡子的时尚。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But Hadrian wears a beard.
sentences.zh: 但哈德良留了胡子。

sentences.en: And in doing this, it exemplifies the twin aspects of his character.
sentences.zh: 这样做体现了他性格的双重性。

sentences.en: Because on the one hand, a beard marks him out as a legionary, as a common soldier.
sentences.zh: 因为一方面，胡子标志着他是一名军团士兵，一名普通士兵。

sentences.en: And he is much loved by the legions.
sentences.zh: 他深受军团的爱戴。

sentences.en: He is a man who has served with them, who does everything that, whatever he asks them to do, he will do it.
sentences.zh: 他是一个与他们并肩作战的人，无论他要求他们做什么，他自己也会去做。

sentences.en: And even though he's building his walls and his palisades and so on, he's doing this.
sentences.zh: 即使他在建造围墙、栅栏等等，他也是亲力亲为。

sentences.en: They're not defensive measures.
sentences.zh: 这些并不是防御措施。

sentences.en: They're kind of expressions of contempt for the barbarians who lie beyond the realms of imperial spectacles.
sentences.zh: 它们更像是对帝国疆域之外那些野蛮人的蔑视。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Basically, what Hadrian is saying is that this world, the world ruled by Rome is a great garden and anyone beyond it, not allowed entrance.
sentences.zh: 基本上，哈德良想说的是，这个世界，由罗马统治的世界是一个大花园，任何在它之外的人，都不允许进入。

sentences.en: So you're kind of beyond the pale.
sentences.zh: 所以你算是被排斥在外了。

sentences.en: And the other aspect of Hadrian's beard is that it marks him out as a philosopher.
sentences.zh: 而哈德良胡子的另一个方面是，它标志着他是一位哲学家。

sentences.en: And Hadrian is a great lover of Greek culture.
sentences.zh: 哈德良非常热爱希腊文化。

sentences.en: As a young man, he was called Greitless.
sentences.zh: 年轻时，他被称为“希腊迷”。

sentences.en: And this devotion to Greece and to Greek culture and to the Greek way of doing things is something that marks him out as very distinctive among Roman emperors.
sentences.zh: 这种对希腊、希腊文化以及希腊行事方式的痴迷，使他在罗马皇帝中显得非常独特。

sentences.en: There hasn't been a Roman emperor who has been so nakedly Philhellenic as
sentences.zh: 还没有哪位罗马皇帝像哈德良这样，

sentences.en: Hadrian.
sentences.zh: 如此赤裸裸地崇尚希腊文化。

sentences.en: Funnily enough, Tom, that's something he has in common with Oscar Wilde, who we're going to be talking about next.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，汤姆，这正是他和我们接下来要谈的奥斯卡·王尔德的共同点。

sentences.en: Anyway, back to the story.
sentences.zh: 总之，回到故事上来。

sentences.en: Well, so the mention of Oscar Wilde brings us on to Antinous, because Oscar Wilde was also very keen
sentences.zh: 嗯，提到奥斯卡·王尔德就把我们引向了安提诺乌斯，因为奥斯卡·王尔德也非常迷恋

sentences.en: on Antinous, whose image is, I mean, you know, there are almost 120 statues of him have survived.
sentences.zh: 安提诺乌斯，他的形象，我的意思是，你知道，现存的关于他的雕像就有近120座。

sentences.en: Crikey.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: He's born in 110, 111.
sentences.zh: 他出生于110年或111年。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In a place called Bithynia, which is the northwest of what is now Turkey, a place called Claudiopolis, which is mostly famous for its cheeses.
sentences.zh: 出生在一个叫比提尼亚的地方，也就是现在土耳其的西北部，一个叫克劳狄奥波利斯的地方，那里主要以奶酪闻名。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: The thing about him is that he is stupefyingly gorgeous.
sentences.zh: 关于他的一点是，他美得令人目瞪口呆。

sentences.en: And I went to an exhibition in Nottingham about devoted to his statues, to his busts and so on.
sentences.zh: 我曾在诺丁汉看过一个专门展示他雕像、半身像等的展览。

sentences.en: And a very famous bust of him got sent from
sentences.zh: 其中一尊非常著名的半身像被从

sentences.en: Paris, from the Louvre.
sentences.zh: 巴黎的卢浮宫送了过来。

sentences.en: And when the curator opened the crate, she saw that there were lipstick marks all over the marble lips of Antinous.
sentences.zh: 当策展人打开板条箱时，她看到安提诺乌斯大理石嘴唇上全是口红印。

sentences.en: So he is, to this day, capable of exciting, strong feeling.
sentences.zh: 所以直到今天，他依然能激发强烈的感情。

sentences.en: Members of the curatorial classes had been snogging the bust of Antinous.
sentences.zh: 策展界的人员竟然在亲吻安提诺乌斯的半身像。

sentences.en: That absolutely confirms all my darkest fears, Tom, about curators.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这完全证实了我对策展人最阴暗的恐惧。

sentences.en: Anyway.
sentences.zh: 总之。

sentences.en: So he is celebrated as the most beautiful young man that anyone has ever seen.
sentences.zh: 所以他被誉为人们见过的最美丽的年轻人。

sentences.en: Everybody admits this.
sentences.zh: 每个人都承认这一点。

sentences.en: And Hadrian loves him for that, but loves him as well, because he seems to have been very intelligent, very smart.
sentences.zh: 哈德良因为这一点爱他，但也因为他似乎非常聪明、非常机敏而爱他。

sentences.en: And again, Hadrian himself inscribes this.
sentences.zh: 而且，哈德良本人也记录了这一点。

sentences.en: He says that his heart was wise, his intelligence, that of a grown man.
sentences.zh: 他说他的内心充满智慧，他的才智如同成年人一般。

sentences.en: So how does Hadrian come across Antinous?
sentences.zh: 那么哈德良是如何遇到安提诺乌斯的呢？

sentences.en: Well, so Hadrian is a great traveler.
sentences.zh: 嗯，哈德良是一位伟大的旅行家。

sentences.en: I mean, that's what he's doing in Britain.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是他在英国所做的事情。

sentences.en: He's, you know, he goes all across the empire.
sentences.zh: 他游历了整个帝国。

sentences.en: And he is in Claudiopolis in Bithynia in one, two, three.
sentences.zh: 他在123年左右到了比提尼亚的克劳狄奥波利斯。

sentences.en: And it's likely that he,
sentences.zh: 很可能他，

sentences.en: so Antinous would have been 13 at this age.
sentences.zh: 当时安提诺乌斯应该只有13岁。

sentences.en: Hadrian seems to have talent spotted him.
sentences.zh: 哈德良似乎看中了这块璞玉。

sentences.en: But Hadrian's almost 50 at that point, Tom.
sentences.zh: 但汤姆，哈德良那时已经快50岁了。

sentences.en: Hadrian is, yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 哈德良是，是的，是的。

sentences.en: By Roman's stance, quite elderly by this point.
sentences.zh: 按罗马人的标准，那时已经相当老了。

sentences.en: Hadrian seems to have sent him to Italy to be educated, be given kind of schooling.
sentences.zh: 哈德良似乎把他送到了意大利接受教育，让他接受某种学校教育。

sentences.en: And when Hadrian comes back to Rome, he seems to have become very, very devoted to Antinous and starts to take him with him on his travels.
sentences.zh: 当哈德良回到罗马时，他似乎对安提诺乌斯变得非常非常痴迷，并开始带他一起旅行。

sentences.en: So late 128, he goes traveling once again, and he is going off with Antinous and also with his wife, Sabina, with whom relations are perhaps understandably a little bit,
sentences.zh: 所以128年年底，他又一次踏上旅程，他带着安提诺乌斯，还有他的妻子萨比娜，他们之间的关系也许可以理解地有点，

sentences.en: a little bit tetchy.
sentences.zh: 有点紧张。

sentences.en: And they go to Greece.
sentences.zh: 他们去了希腊。

sentences.en: And Hadrian spends a fair while there in Athens.
sentences.zh: 哈德良在雅典待了相当长的一段时间。

sentences.en: He goes with Antinous to Eleusis, to the great mysteries.
sentences.zh: 他带着安提诺乌斯去了厄琉西斯，参加了伟大的秘仪。

sentences.en: And these mysteries are about death and resurrection, about winter and summer, the idea that eternal life can be won.
sentences.zh: 这些秘仪是关于死亡与复活、关于冬与夏，关于永生可以获得的理念。

sentences.en: This is seen as the great gift of
sentences.zh: 这被视为雅典给予世界的伟大礼物。

sentences.en: Athens to the world.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，哈德良与安提诺乌斯分享这些秘仪，是他们之间的一种额外纽带。

sentences.en: So the fact that Hadrian shares these mysteries with Antinous is a kind of extra bond between them, I think.
sentences.zh: 哈德良建立了这种类似于欧洲联盟的希腊版本，称为“泛希腊联盟”。

sentences.en: And Hadrian sets up this kind of Greek equivalent of the European
sentences.zh: 这是一个以雅典为总部的希腊城市联盟。

sentences.en: Union called the Panhellenion.
sentences.zh: 这一切都表达了哈德良对希腊理想的忠诚。

sentences.en: It's this kind of confederation of Greek cities with its headquarters in Athens.
sentences.zh: 我能在这里问你一个简短的问题吗？

sentences.en: And it's all expressive of the way that the Hadrian is devoted to the ideal of Greece.
sentences.zh: 罗马人对他在希腊搞的这些名堂，还有留胡子之类的行为怎么看？

sentences.en: Can I just ask you a quick question at this point?
sentences.zh: 他们能接受吗？

sentences.en: What do people in Rome think about all this carrying on in Greece and, you know, wearing beards and stuff?
sentences.zh: 他们只是觉得，好吧，皇帝是老大，那就随他去吧。

sentences.en: Are they okay with it?
sentences.zh: 还是有些人私下嘀咕，说这一切有点奇怪？

sentences.en: They just think, well, the emperor's the boss, so fine, let him crack on.
sentences.zh: 肯定有保守的罗马人不喜欢它。

sentences.en: Or are some people muttering and saying, this is all a bit weird?
sentences.zh: 我认为其中最杰出的是塔西佗，他——

sentences.en: There are definitely conservative Romans who dislike it.
sentences.zh: 我得在节目里提一下，塔西佗。

sentences.en: And I think the most eminent of these is Tacitus, who's-
sentences.zh: 早期罗马帝国的伟大历史学家。

sentences.en: I'd say in front of the show, Tacitus.
sentences.zh: 我认为他笔下的提比略，那个热爱希腊文化、最终变得嗜杀且堕落的独裁者，实际上是对哈德良的一种恶毒的讽刺画像。

sentences.en: The great historian of early imperial Rome.
sentences.zh: 我认为——

sentences.en: And I think his portrait of Tiberius, which is of a Greek culture-loving autocrat who ends up murderous and depraved, is a kind of vicious pen portrait of Hadrian, actually.
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: I think-
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是这样。

sentences.en: That is.
sentences.zh: 但罗马帝国已经变了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 它正变得非常非常多元文化。

sentences.en: But the Roman Empire has changed.
sentences.zh: 希腊人正在进入元老院。

sentences.en: It's becoming very, very kind of multicultural.
sentences.zh: 他们正在成为执政官。

sentences.en: Greeks are entering the Senate.
sentences.zh: 这种正在变成希腊-罗马世界的感觉，是哈德良正在驾驭的一股浪潮。

sentences.en: They're becoming consuls.
sentences.zh: 所以，这并不是说——当然，它在罗马引起了抱怨，但这些抱怨对他没有任何威胁。

sentences.en: The sense that this is becoming a Greco-Roman world is a wave that Hadrian is surfing.
sentences.zh: 而且希腊人爱他。

sentences.en: So it's not, I mean, of course it generates grumbles in Rome, but not grumbles that are in any way threatening to him.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，可以理解，想象一下。

sentences.en: And the Greeks love him.
sentences.zh: 他抵达亚历山大港时，带着安提诺乌斯。

sentences.en: I mean, understandably, imagine that.
sentences.zh: 对于亚历山大港的希腊人来说，就像在雅典一样，他带着这位希腊情人，被视为哈德良尊重他们整个文化的一个标志。

sentences.en: And he arrives in Alexandria and he has Antinous with him.
sentences.zh: 当他们到达亚历山大港时，那是在130年，安提诺乌斯19岁了。

sentences.en: And for the Greeks in Alexandria, as in Athens, the fact that he has this kind of Greek lover with him is taken as a marker of Hadrian's respect for their entire culture.
sentences.zh: 所以他开始练出肌肉了。

sentences.en: And by the time that they reach Alexandria, which is in 130, Antinous is 19.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他的下巴开始长出胡茬了。

sentences.en: So he's putting on muscles.
sentences.zh: 他开始看起来像那种会出去参加狮子狩猎的少年了。
